lead: Canthal tilt tape, also called lateral eye lift tape or fox eye tape, is a temporary cosmetic aid in which a strip of tape is placed near the outer corner of the eye and pulled toward the temple to angle the outer corner upward. The aim is to give the eyes a more lifted, almond or 'fox' shape for photos, events or daily wear, without surgery.

The canthi are the corners where the upper and lower eyelids meet. The lateral canthus is the outer corner and is sharper in angle, with the lids lying close against the eyeball; the medial canthus is the inner corner.[1] The line through both canthi, the bicanthal plane, marks the upper boundary of the midface.[1] Canthal tilt describes how far the outer corner sits above or below the inner corner, and a positive (upward) tilt is a feature frequently praised in looksmaxxing discussion.[2]

Wikipedia notes that looksmaxxing communities admire 'hunter eyes', a look associated with a positive canthal tilt, little or no upper eyelid showing and low-set eyebrows.[2] Tape is a non-permanent way to imitate part of that look. The permanent alternative in clinical practice is canthoplasty, a plastic surgery on the corner of the eye done for cosmetic reasons or to correct lid position.[1]

paras: The canthus is the corner where the eyelids meet. The inner and outer canthi mark the ends of the palpebral fissure.[1] In many East Asian and some Southeast Asian people a fold of skin, the epicanthic fold, partly covers the inner corner, while in other populations the inner corner is typically fully exposed.[1]
Canthoplasty is plastic surgery on the medial or lateral canthus, performed for cosmetic reasons or to correct eyelid function or malposition.[1]

Looksmaxxing discussion rates the eye area highly, and Wikipedia describes 'hunter eyes' as a coveted male look tied to positive canthal tilt, minimal upper eyelid exposure and low-set brows, compared by enthusiasts to a predator's gaze.[2] People who want that look try methods ranging from mewing to surgery.[2] Tape is a low-commitment, reversible way to see the effect of a lifted outer corner.

quick.overview:
Canthal tilt tape is adhesive tape stuck near the outer corner of the eye and pulled back toward the temple, so the outer corner sits higher. In looksmaxxing vocabulary a more upward-angled outer corner is called positive canthal tilt.

The sources reviewed contain no studies of the tape. This entry therefore covers definitions only.
quick.mechanism: The tape holds the skin at the lateral canthus under tension, which is intended to raise the apparent position of the outer corner relative to the inner corner. The effect is temporary and ends when the tape is removed.
quick.risks: No studies of safety or effectiveness were found. Adhesive and skin tension near the eye are general considerations that have not been tested for this product.
